arxiv-2012-10496.title: Factorization of Binary Matrices: Rank Relations, Uniqueness and Model Selection of Boolean Decomposition
arxiv-2012-10496.creator: Derek DeSantis, Erik Skau, Duc P. Truong, Boian Alexandrov
arxiv-2012-10496.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Derek DeSantis, Erik Skau, Duc P. Truong, Boian Alexandrov. The application of binary matrices are numerous. Representing a matrix as a mixture of a small collection of latent vectors via low-rank decomposition is often seen as an advantageous method to interpret and analyze data. In this work, we examine the factorizations of binary matrices using standard arithmetic (real and nonnegative) and logical operations (Boolean and ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} ). We examine the relationships between the different ranks, and discuss when factorization is unique.

arxiv-2105-08272.creator: Guanlin Li, Yao Yao
arxiv-2105-08272.description: Abstract . We study a system of PDEs modeling the population dynamics of two competitive species whose spatial movements are governed by both diffusion and mutually repulsive chemotaxis effects. We prove that solutions to this system are globally well-posed, without any smallness assumptions on the chemotactic coefficients.

arxiv-2309-15962.creator: Michelle Daher, Mark Powell
arxiv-2309-15962.description: Abstract . We show that every locally flat topological embedding of a 3-manifold in a smooth 5-manifold is homotopic, by a small homotopy, to a smooth embedding. arxiv-2312-12497.title: Resurgence of large order relations
arxiv-2312-12497.creator: Coenraad Marinissen, Alexander van Spaendonck, and Marcel Vonk
arxiv-2312-12497.description: Abstract One of the main applications of resurgence in physics is the decoding of nonperturbative effects through large order relations. These relations connect perturbative asymptotic expansions of observables to expansions around other saddle points. Together, this data is unified in transseries that describe the nonperturbative structure. It is known that large order relations themselves also take the form of transseries.

Key to such analyses are the different parameters of each model, which affect various network features, such as its size, clustering, or degree distribution. arxiv-2404-14570.title: Approximating Korobov Functions via Quantum Circuits
arxiv-2404-14570.creator: Junaid Aftab, Haizhao Yang
arxiv-2404-14570.description: Abstract . Approximation theory provides a useful framework for assessing the expressive capacity and computational complexity of quantum circuits. In this work, we design quantum circuits that approximate d d -dimensional functions in the Korobov function space. Our construction combines quantum signal processing (QSP) with the linear combination of unitaries (LCU) method to implement circuits that generate Chebyshev polynomials.

arxiv-2404-17221.creator: Marco Peer, Florian Kleber, Robert Sablatnig
arxiv-2404-17221.description: Abstract This paper introduces Saghog , a self-supervised pretraining strategy for writer retrieval using HOG features of the binarized input image. Our preprocessing involves the application of the Segment Anything technique to extract handwriting from various datasets, ending up with about 24k documents, followed by training a vision transformer on reconstructing masked patches of the handwriting.

arxiv-2602-20300.creator: William Watson, Nicole Cho, Sumitra Ganesh, Manuela Veloso
arxiv-2602-20300.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by William Watson, Nicole Cho, Sumitra Ganesh, Manuela Veloso. Large Language Model (LLM) hallucinations are usually treated as defects of the model or its decoding strategy. Drawing on classical linguistics, we argue that a query’s form can also shape a listener’s (and model’s) response. We operationalize this insight by constructing a 17-dimension query feature vector covering clause complexity, lexical rarity, and anaphora, negation, answerability, and intention grounding, all known to affect human comprehension.
